findings.title: Async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch dead and turns deletion failures into unhandled rejections
findings.body: The callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` was changed to `async` so it can `await getCalendar(...)`, but `forEach` does not collect or return the promises produced by an async callback. The `try { ... } catch` block wrapping the loop (lines 124–139) can therefore no longer catch anything: any synchronous throw that the catch previously handled (e.g. a CalendarService constructor error from `new CalendarService(credential)` inside `getCalendar`) and any rejection from the dynamic import, `calendar.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` now escapes as an unhandled promise rejection, which crashes Node ≥15 server processes by default and never reaches the `logger.error` path. Additionally, because the callback suspends at the first `await getCalendar(...)`, the `deleteEvent` calls are not even initiated before the function moves on to send the reschedule email and return `true`; in a serverless environment the function can finish (and be frozen) before the calendar/video deletions ever run, leaving stale events on users' calendars while the booking is already marked CANCELLED. Fix by replacing the forEach with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` inside the try block.

findings.title: Async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch dead and turns deletion failures into unhandled rejections
findings.body: Same issue as in packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts: the `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` loop (lines 124–139) discards the promises from its async callback, so the enclosing `try/catch` can no longer catch errors that it previously caught synchronously (e.g. CalendarService constructor failures), and every failure — dynamic import rejection, `calendar.deleteEvent` rejection, `deleteMeeting` rejection — becomes an unhandled promise rejection that bypasses the `logger.error` handling and can crash the Node process. The function also proceeds to send the reschedule email and return `true` without waiting for any calendar or video deletion to complete; because the callback now suspends at `await getCalendar(...)` before `deleteEvent` is even invoked, the deletions may never start if the serverless invocation ends with the response, leaving stale events on external calendars for a booking already marked CANCELLED. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` inside the try.

findings.title: requestReschedule: deletions are fire-and-forget; failures are now unhandled rejections instead of thrown errors
findings.body: In the `requestReschedule` mutation, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) ... })` discards all async callback results. Before this change a synchronous failure in `getCalendar` (e.g. a CalendarService constructor throwing) propagated out of the mutation and produced a visible error; now it, and any dynamic-import rejection, becomes an unhandled promise rejection (a crash risk on Node ≥15). Also, since the callback suspends at `await getCalendar` before calling `deleteEvent`, the calendar/video deletions are not even started before the reschedule email is sent and the mutation returns — if the serverless function is frozen after responding, the old event is never removed from the external calendar/meeting provider even though the booking was already marked cancelled and rescheduled. The loop should be `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` (ideally with per-item `.catch` logging) so deletions complete and errors are handled before responding.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now embeds an unawaited Promise in the `calendar` field and discards promises for non-calendar variants
findings.body: `getCalendarCredentials` is still a synchronous function but now calls the newly-async `getCalendar(credential)` without awaiting it, so the returned objects carry `calendar: Promise<Calendar | null>` where callers previously received `Calendar | null`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` (updated in this PR) awaits that field; any other consumer of this exported helper that touches `item.calendar` synchronously will now operate on a Promise instead of a Calendar and break at runtime, and the `ReturnType<typeof getCalendarCredentials>` contract changed silently. Additionally, `getCalendar(credential)` is invoked before the `app.variant === "calendar"` check, so for non-calendar-variant apps the promise is created and immediately discarded — a rejection of that dynamic import would be an unhandled rejection. Make the function async, resolve with `Promise.all`, and only call `getCalendar` for credentials that are actually returned.

findings.title: Dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly, so all apps are still loaded on module evaluation
findings.body: The object literal evaluates each `import("./applecalendar")` etc. immediately when `packages/app-store/index.ts` is first imported, so every consumer of `@calcom/app-store` still triggers loading all 28 app bundles — just asynchronously instead of synchronously. Any code path that needs a single app (e.g. `getCalendar` for one credential type) pays the module-loading cost for all of them, so the change adds asynchrony without delivering the lazy-loading/startup benefit the PR title implies, and on serverless cold starts everything is still fetched and evaluated. If per-app lazy loading is the goal, store thunks or use lazy getters (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and only invoke the one that is needed.
